title: Why Event Planners Are Walking Away From Jobs They Love
summary: The events industry attracts people who love their jobs — and companies have learned to treat that love as a substitute for pay, staffing, and sleep.

title: Sponsorship Tiers Are Dying. Outcome-Based Packages Are Catching On.
summary: The tier chart was never about the sponsor. It was about saving time. Crypto events are trading that convenience for more work — and, they'd argue, a better return.

title: Why One Destination Is Giving Junior Planners a Seat at the Table
summary: A DMO handing emerging planners equal footing with their veteran counterparts is a bet that the next generation’s priorities are worth building around before they’re actually signing contracts.

title: The Fake Conference Problem Is Getting Much Worse
summary: For organizers, the fight isn’t just about protecting the official event website anymore. Brand monitoring across domains, ads, and social accounts is becoming as essential as registration security itself.

title: When a Hotel Walks Away, Most Planners Still Can’t Calculate the Real Cost
summary: Contract language protects an organization's right to be made whole. It doesn't produce the number that proves what "whole" means.

title: How One Meetings Leader Turned a Creative Background Into a Strategy Playbook
summary: An art history degree may seem an unlikely path to leading global meetings strategy at a medical technology company. It’s also a reminder that the job increasingly demands storytellers, not just logistics experts.

title: Incentive Planners Count on CVBs, But Few Bureaus Are Staffing for Them
summary: The funding model for a CVB means they have to focus on the biggest pieces of business. But incentive planners rely on their expertise, too.

title: Conference Safety Guidelines: What 10 Event Organizers Include
summary: Conference safety guidelines do more than keep attendees safe. They protect the event organizer from liability.

title: The Event Industry's AI Problem Isn't AI
summary: The seamless AI-powered event isn't waiting on better technology. It's waiting on organizers, sponsors, and attendees to trust each other with the data that makes it work.

title: Bending Spoons Keeps Buying: $1.285 Billion for Airtable This Time
summary: Bending Spoons now owns a registration platform and planning tool that many event teams run on daily. The company's track record says cost discipline comes before product investment, which means the integration organizers are hoping for is a bet, not a guarantee.
